variables.name: Stance
variables.instructions:
Code the position of the person writing the post, not of people the post quotes or describes.
- Sarcasm counts as the position it implies. "Brilliant plan." after a complaint is Oppose.
- Supporting bikes in general while rejecting this plan is Oppose.
- A question or a news update with no position is Neutral or unclear.

categories.name: Support
categories.definition: The post favors the proposal or argues for building the lanes.

categories.name: Oppose
categories.definition: The post is against the proposal or argues it should not go ahead as planned.

categories.name: Neutral or unclear
categories.definition: The post takes no position, only shares information or asks a question, or its position cannot be determined.
examples: Not sure how I feel about this one yet.

worked_examples.text: Oh sure, let's spend millions so twelve people can bike to brunch.
worked_examples.reason: Sarcasm. The implied position is against the proposal.

worked_examples.text: I love cycling, but this design puts the lane on the wrong side of the street. Send it back.
worked_examples.reason: Supports biking in general but rejects this plan.

worked_examples.text: Does the proposal include the bridge section?

variables.name: Primary frame
variables.instructions:
Choose the one consideration the post spends the most words on.
- If two frames get equal weight, choose the one mentioned first.
- A post that only cheers or boos, with no reason given, is Other or none.

categories.name: Safety
categories.definition: Injuries, deaths, crashes, speeding, emergency access, or feeling safe on the street.
examples: Two cyclists were killed on Main Street in five years.

categories.name: Economy
categories.definition: Business revenue, parking for customers, costs, taxes, property values, or household budgets.
examples: Shops on streets with bike lanes see more foot traffic.

categories.name: Environment and health
categories.definition: Climate, emissions, air quality, noise, or public health effects of traffic.
examples: Fewer cars downtown means cleaner air.

categories.name: Fairness and process
categories.definition: Who was consulted, who benefits or is left out, accessibility, or how the decision was made.
examples: They held ONE public meeting, at 2pm on a weekday.

categories.name: Other or none
categories.definition: None of the frames above is emphasized, including purely informational posts and general praise or dislike.
examples: Does anyone know if the lanes will connect to the river trail?

worked_examples.text: It would make the street safer, and honestly it would also help the shops.
worked_examples.reason: Two frames with equal weight. Safety is mentioned first.

variables.name: Incivility
variables.instructions:
Look for attacks on people, not on ideas.
- Calling a plan stupid is Absent. Calling the people behind it stupid is Present.
- Sarcasm and anger alone are Absent.

categories.name: Present
categories.definition: Name-calling, insults, or demeaning language aimed at a person or group.
examples: Anyone who thinks this is a good idea is a complete idiot.

categories.name: Absent
categories.definition: No insults or demeaning language aimed at people, even if the tone is angry or sarcastic.
examples: Hard no. Main Street is for cars.

worked_examples.text: This is the dumbest plan the city has ever produced.
worked_examples.reason: The insult is aimed at the plan, not at people.

worked_examples.text: The planners who drew this up are clueless fools.
